evidence_projection.inference_boundary: Affected provider, product, model, and runtime identity is projected from structured system_or_product and model_or_algorithm source metadata, with bounded fallback to an existing concrete FM system_context for older records. source_platform identifies where evidence is hosted or published and is not treated as affected-system identity. failure_mode_definition: A failure in which untrusted model-produced or data-plane state crosses into trusted agent-framework control state and is interpreted, loaded, routed or executed as configuration, tool schema, checkpoint, serialized object, cache, memory policy, orchestration instruction or equivalent control-plane material without fresh provenance and authority validation.
failure_threshold: The threshold requires a framework or orchestration boundary, attacker-influenced model/data-plane state, conversion into or execution as trusted control state, and a security-relevant consequence or credible pathway. Model-context prompt injection with no framework transition and transformation laundering with no control-plane crossing are excluded.

failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S1 reflects demonstrated paths from prompt-controlled state into framework or host execution, including remote code execution, while the cited disclosures are authorised research and do not establish widespread malicious exploitation.
failure_classification.likelihood: demonstrated in controlled security research; recurrence depends on deployment architecture and control coverage
failure_classification.confidence: high for the demonstrated mechanism; bounded for undisclosed provider internals and ecosystem prevalence
failure_classification.failure_scope: agent frameworks, orchestration, checkpoints, memory, routing, serialization and tools
failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: May recur wherever frameworks treat model/data outputs as trusted control objects or parameters without independent validation.
failure_classification.persistence: May be transient or persist in checkpoints, caches or memory; persistence is not required.
failure_classification.reproducibility: Testable through authorised tainted-state cases across serializers, checkpoints, routing, tool schemas and orchestration handlers.
failure_classification.visibility: Often hidden beneath fluent model behaviour; may surface only as framework, tool or host effects.
